name: Interpol
label: Matador
lede: A philosophy-class pickup, a drummer rescued from a vintage clothing store and a bassist who became a cult figure: Interpol made the New York record of 2002, left for a major, came crawling back, and ended up playing to 160,000 people in Mexico City.

eras.title: A band with no name
eras.text: Daniel Kessler had wanted a band for a while and assembled one from NYU and the East Village. For three years Interpol drew decent crowds and self-released EPs, and swapped out a drummer who belonged to the screamo scene.

years.h: Daniel Kessler recruits Carlos Dengler after a philosophy class
years.p: At NYU, Daniel Kessler approaches Carlos Dengler after class, drawn by his look. He then runs into [[Paul Banks|71db5060-324e-4cc5-8ca6-0070220ae000]] in the East Village, and Greg Drudy takes the drums.
years.xp: Dengler was headed for academia and bass wasn't his main instrument, but he said yes. For a while the band had crowds but no name: Las Armas and The French Letters were both considered before Interpol stuck.

years.h: Greg Drudy leaves; Sam Fogarino comes in from a vintage store
years.p: Greg Drudy goes to [[Hot Cross|7210704b-06de-42ee-beb6-44e65357b12e]], [[Saetia|cd4f7c44-9ff3-4660-9f93-170fef83edfd]] and his label Level Plane. Sam Fogarino, working at a vintage clothing shop and thinking of quitting music, replaces him.

years.h: Glasgow's Chemikal Underground puts out Interpol first
years.p: Interpol appears on Fukd ID No. 3, an EP in the Scottish label Chemikal Underground's series, two years before any American label signs them.

eras.title: Bright lights, dark suits
eras.text: Recorded in Connecticut with Peter Katis and released on Matador Records, Turn On the Bright Lights made Interpol the band everyone compared to Joy Division and everyone else compared to Interpol.

years.h: Interpol records its debut at Tarquin Studios, Connecticut
years.p: Producer Peter Katis tracks Turn On the Bright Lights in Bridgeport. The songs were written before September 11, but the attacks changed how the band heard them.

years.h: Interpol signs to Matador
years.p: Interpol joins Matador, part of the independent Beggars Group. A June EP, Interpol, carries re-recorded versions of PDA and NYC.

years.h: Turn On the Bright Lights · Pitchfork's No. 1 of 2002
years.p: Out August 19 in the UK and a day later in the US. It spends 73 weeks on Billboard's independent chart and eventually goes gold in both countries.
years.xp: According to Wikipedia's certification figures it reached about 522,000 in the US and roughly a million worldwide. The Killers, Editors and the xx have all been named as bands it shaped.

years.big: Album of the year. Dud of the month.
years.h: Robert Christgau names the album Dud of the Month
years.p: The same record Pitchfork crowned best of 2002 got Robert Christgau's Dud of the Month in the Village Voice.

eras.title: The cult of Carlos D
eras.text: Antics brought UK hits, stadium support slots and eighteen months on the road. It also made the bassist a Lower East Side style icon and wore the band out.

years.h: Antics sells 350,000 in four months
years.p: Back at Tarquin Studios for the follow-up. Slow Hands, Evil and C'mere all reach the UK Top 40 and the album goes gold in the UK and US.

years.h: URB's cover story: Interpol + The Cult of Carlos D
years.p: Carlos Dengler's leather and styled look make him the face of the band. By 2007 he drops the look and says it felt good to be unrecognized.

years.h: Interpol opens for U2 and The Cure, and hits the wall
years.p: Near the end of an 18-month Antics tour, Interpol tells Radio 1's Zane Lowe at a Sunderland show how exhausted it is. Direction lands on a Six Feet Under soundtrack.

years.h: Interpol leaves Matador for Capitol Records
years.p: Reports that Interpol has signed to major label Capitol are confirmed by Matador on September 1.

eras.title: Major label, minor misery
eras.text: The Capitol album was the band's biggest chart hit and, by Banks's account, its worst experience. Then the bassist quit, Interpol went back to Matador, and a borrowed bassist from Slint passed through.

q: the worst experience the band ever had working on an album
years.h: Our Love to Admire hits No. 4, and hurts
years.p: Interpol's first New York-recorded album, made with Rich Costey at Electric Lady and the Magic Shop, peaks at No. 4 in the US and No. 2 in the UK.
years.xp: Banks told Vice that major-label pressure was to blame. Keyboards were in from the start for the first time; Kessler called them a fifth member. Interpol headlined Lollapalooza in Chicago that August.

years.h: Paul Banks goes solo as Julian Plenti
years.p: Paul Banks releases Julian Plenti is... Skyscraper under an assumed name, mixed by Peter Katis at Tarquin.

years.h: Carlos Dengler leaves Interpol after the fourth album
years.p: The band's website announces Carlos Dengler is out. Sam Fogarino later says Dengler was tired of touring and of bass, never his preferred instrument. David Pajo of Slint covers on tour.
years.xp: Dengler later earned an MFA in drama from NYU's Tisch School and staged an autobiographical one-man show, Homo Sapiens Interruptus, at the 2016 New York Fringe.

years.h: Interpol: back on Matador after Capitol
years.p: Management changes at Capitol send Interpol back to Matador for its self-titled fourth album, Carlos Dengler's last.

years.h: David Pajo leaves; Brad Truax takes the bass
years.p: David Pajo steps away to spend time with his family, and Brad Truax takes over on tour. That July, Interpol opens for U2 at Chicago's Soldier Field.

years.h: After Reading and Leeds, Interpol takes a break
years.p: Sam Fogarino says the band needs a big break, and the members scatter into side projects, including Paul Banks's second solo album.

eras.title: Banks picks up the bass
eras.text: Down to a trio, Interpol stopped trying to replace Dengler in the studio: Banks played bass himself. The ten-year-old debut became a victory lap.

years.h: Turn On the Bright Lights gets a 10th-anniversary edition
years.p: The remaster adds demos, live cuts and the hard-to-find Get the Girls and Cubed.

years.h: El Pintor, an anagram of Interpol
years.p: Paul Banks came up with the title while sketching merchandise. He plays bass on the record; Brandon Curtis of The Secret Machines plays keys.

years.h: Interpol's bus is snowed in at Buffalo for 50 hours
years.p: A snowstorm traps the El Pintor tour in Buffalo, New York, for more than 50 hours. Two Canadian shows and one in Boston are postponed.

years.h: Interpol plays Turn On the Bright Lights in full
years.p: A 15th-anniversary tour plays the debut from start to finish.

years.h: Marauder, announced at a Mexico City press conference
years.p: Interpol announces its sixth album in Mexico City in June, with The Rover as the first single.

years.h: Our Love to Admire vanishes from streaming
years.p: A licensing dispute pulls the Capitol album off streaming services. Paul Banks tells fans on Twitter to hang tight.

eras.title: The biggest room they ever played
eras.text: Matador bought back the whole catalog, and the band turned into a stadium act in Latin America. In 2026 the touring bassist and keyboardist finally became members.

years.h: Matador acquires Interpol's entire back catalog
years.p: Matador now owns all of it, including Our Love to Admire, ending the licensing mess.

years.h: The Other Side of Make-Believe, written in the Catskills
years.p: Begun over the internet during the pandemic, then written in a Catskills house and recorded in London with Flood and Alan Moulder.

years.h: Sam Fogarino sits out for spinal surgery
years.p: Chris Broome fills in on drums while Sam Fogarino recovers from spinal surgery.

years.h: 160,000 people at Mexico City's Zócalo
years.p: Interpol plays a free show in Mexico City's main square to an estimated 160,000, its biggest crowd ever, then tours Antics in full for its 20th anniversary.

years.h: Brandon Curtis and Brad Truax become official members
years.p: Announcing This Mirror Weighs a Ton on Partisan Records, Paul Banks says Brad Truax wrote and played the basslines. Urian Hackney, then [[The Walkmen|b7834ebd-64ae-46c3-a930-2d3a52ee743a]]'s Matt Barrick, drum on tour.

years.h: This Mirror Weighs a Ton, the eighth album
years.p: Interpol's first album on Partisan Records, with Sam Fogarino contributing and Curtis and Truax credited as members.
